predecessors.name: Magadha
predecessors.text: janapada-of-magadha's last shape (its -530 correction, 107 cells, about 28,000 km2): Magadha with Anga after Bimbisara's annexation: 'Anga was annexed by Magadha in the time of Bimbisara'; the…

successors.name: Shaishunaga dynasty
successors.text: Magadha under Shishunaga, who overthrew the last Haryanka

ledger.x: 500 BCE: Magadha is drawn as the Haryanka kingdom of Bimbisara.
481 BCE: Ajatashatru's second campaign against the Vajjika League.
480 BCE: Cliopatria's shape grows from 33,403 to 93,608 km2; 251 cells are new against keyframe 0.
468 BCE: Ajatashatru annexes the Vajjika League.
468 BCE: the Mallas pass to Magadha with the league.
460 BCE: the court moves from Rajagriha to Pataliputra.
450 BCE: Cliopatria's -450 shape adds 500 cells (bbox 80.94-88.53E 21.49-27.74N, about 130000 km2) beyond keyframe 2 and the Kosala-Kasi land.

wars.name: Magadha-Vajji war
wars.outcome: Magadha wins: Ajatashatru annexes the Vajjika League (Licchavi, Videha, Naya) and the Mallas by 468 BCE, after a decade of diplomacy and intrigue.

wars.name: Magadha-Kosala war over Kashi
wars.outcome: After Bimbisara's murder Prasenajit took Kashi back; the war ended in a peace treaty and Prasenajit's daughter Vajira's marriage to Ajatashatru; Ajatashatru later occupied Kashi and Kasi-Kosala.

certainty.note: No border of this period rests on a treaty or survey; the rivers (Ganga, Gandaki, Mahananda) bound the Vajji country but the page gives no frontier lines for Magadha, and the southern fringe in Cliopatria's shapes is unverified.
